attributions.reason: The recomputed frozen pixel sample lies in a solid, glyph-free side strip of the actual fully visible disabled primary button, with suitable dominant support. The original PNG visibly dims the entire button fill and text. Source defines the approved disabled palette value on the label background but applies native disabled behavior to the plain SwiftUI button; the rendered disabled treatment changes that owned surface. The sampled region is the component action, not the host or a text leaf, so this is a product rendered-style defect, not an unsuitable observation. The precise platform compositing mechanism is inferred from source plus visible disabled treatment; the strict pixel contradiction itself is recomputed.

The caller advances in the same process to fixture 1 (revision bicycle-1), whose actual incoming initialSelectedIDs is [b]; the updated notice is visibly present and stable input/epoch bindings agree. Nevertheless the component shows neither service selected, No work selected / 0 min, and a disabled primary button. The component’s revision-driven state handling fails the authoritative incoming selection. This same product behavior explains the summary, enablement and disabled action-fill failures; they are not independent root causes. Source-a’s SwiftUI state/onChange implementation owns resetting selection; no host input or screenshot-epoch failure is evidenced.

The original fixture-1 frames show only a selected and its 20-minute summary even though the authoritative replacement selected b and the later a action adds a. The demonstrated native a toggle emits bicycle:toggle:a:true, establishing that a is being added after the replacement rather than deselected. The component has lost b during revision replacement; the continued summary/callback failures are manifestations of that product state defect. Source, changed notice, actual fixture and stable native bindings establish that the caller update reached the live component. This assessment does not infer a handler from a label or a blocked disabled action.
